paragraphs: Home BancShares, Inc. ("Home BancShares," "we," "us," "HBI" or the "Company") is a Conway, Arkansas headquartered bank holding company registered under the federal Bank Holding Company Act of 1956. The Company's common stock is traded through the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "HOMB." We are primarily engaged in providing a broad range of commercial and retail banking and related financial services to businesses, real estate developers and investors, individuals and municipalities through our wholly owned community bank subsidiary – Centennial Bank. Centennial Bank has branch locations in Arkansas, Florida, Texas, South Alabama and New York City. Although the Company has a diversified loan portfolio, at December 31, 2025 and 2024, commercial real estate loans represented 53.2% and 57.6% of gross loans and 194.3% and 214.6% of total stockholders' equity, respectively. The Company's total assets, total deposits, total revenue and net income for each of the past three years are as follows:
Total revenue (net interest income plus non-interest income) 1,090,869 1,017,348 996,879 Net income 475,441 402,241 392,929

Home BancShares acquires, organizes and invests in community banks that serve attractive markets. Our community banking team is built around experienced bankers with strong local relationships. The Company was formed in 1998 by an investor group led by John W. Allison, our Chairman, and Robert H. "Bunny" Adcock, Jr., one of our directors. Since opening our first subsidiary bank in 1999, we have acquired and integrated a total of 23 banks with locations in Arkansas, Florida, Texas and Alabama, including 18 banks since 2010, seven of which we acquired through Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC") assisted transactions. Our subsidiary bank has operated under a single charter and the Centennial Bank name since 2009. In 2015, after acquiring a pool of national commercial real estate loans, we created Centennial Commercial Finance Group ("Centennial CFG") to build out a national lending platform focused on commercial real estate as well as commercial and industrial loans. Centennial CFG operates out of our New York City branch office and loan production offices in Los Angeles, California, and Dallas, Texas. In 2018, we acquired Shore Premier Finance ("SPF"), a marine-lending division of Union Bank & Trust of Richmond, Virginia, and established the SPF division of Centennial Bank to build out a lending platform focusing on commercial and consumer marine loans. In 2020, we acquired LH-Finance, the marine lending division of People's United Bank, N.A. of Bridgeport, Connecticut, and consolidated LH-Finance and its loan portfolio with our SPF division. The SPF division operates out of loan production offices in Chesapeake, Virginia and Baltimore, Maryland. In 2022, we completed our largest acquisition to-date and first in the state of Texas with the acquisition of Happy Bancshares, Inc. and its bank subsidiary, Happy State Bank, headquartered in Amarillo, Texas, on April 1, 2022.

We believe many individuals and businesses prefer banking with a locally managed community bank capable of providing flexibility and quick decisions. The execution of our community banking strategy has allowed us to rapidly build our network of banking operations through acquisitions. The following summary provides additional details concerning our acquisitions during the previous five fiscal years.

LendingClub Bank Marine Portfolio – On February 4, 2022, the Company completed the purchase of the performing marine loan portfolio of Utah-based LendingClub Bank ("LendingClub"). Under the terms of the purchase agreement with LendingClub, the Company acquired approximately $242.2 million of yacht loans. This portfolio of loans is housed within the Company's SPF division, which is responsible for servicing the acquired loan portfolio and originating new loan production.

Happy Bancshares, Inc. – On April 1, 2022, the Company completed the acquisition of Happy Bancshares, Inc. ("Happy"), and merged Happy State Bank into Centennial Bank. The Company issued approximately 42.4 million shares of its common stock valued at approximately $958.8 million as of April 1, 2022. In addition, the holders of certain Happy stock-based awards received approximately $3.7 million in cash in cancellation of such awards, for a total transaction value of approximately $962.5 million.

Including the purchase accounting adjustments, as of the acquisition date, Happy had approximately $6.69 billion in total assets, $3.65 billion in loans and $5.86 billion in customer deposits. Happy formerly operated its banking business from 62 locations in Texas.

For additional discussions regarding the acquisition of Happy, see Note 2 "Business Combinations" in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024.

Mountain Commerce Bancorp, Inc. – On December 7, 2025, the Company and Centennial entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "Agreement") with Mountain Commerce Bancorp, Inc., a Tennessee Corporation ("MCBI"), and its wholly-owned bank subsidiary, Mountain Commerce Bank, a Tennessee state banking corporation ("MCB"), under which the Company and Centennial will acquire MCBI and MCB. The Agreement provides that, in a series of transactions, an acquisition subsidiary of the Company will merge into MCBI and MCBI will merge into the Company, with the Company as the surviving entity (collectively, the "Merger"). As soon as reasonably practicable following the Merger, MCB will merge into Centennial, with Centennial as the surviving entity.

Under the terms of the Agreement, the Company will issue approximately 5.4 million shares of its common stock to the shareholders of MCBI upon completion of the Merger. No cash consideration will be paid in connection with the Merger, except that holders of outstanding shares of MCBI common stock at the time of the Merger will receive cash payments in lieu of any fractional shares of Company common stock to which they are otherwise entitled in connection with the Merger.

Subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the Agreement, at the effective time of the Merger (the "Effective Time"), each outstanding share of common stock of MCBI will be converted into the right to receive, without interest, 0.85 shares of the Company's common stock (the "Merger Consideration"). Each unvested restricted share of MCBI common stock outstanding at the Effective Time will fully vest and be converted into the right to receive Merger Consideration. The Merger Consideration value will be determined using a volume-weighted average closing price of the Company's common stock as reported on the New York Stock Exchange over the 20 consecutive trading day period ending on the third business day prior to the closing of the Merger ("the Company's Average Closing Price"), multiplied by 0.85.
The Merger is expected to close in the second quarter of 2026 and is subject to regulatory approvals and other conditions set forth in the Agreement.

headings: Risks Related to Our Industry
We are subject to heightened regulatory requirements as our total assets exceed $10 billion.
Difficult market and economic conditions may adversely affect our industry and our business.
Our FDIC insurance premiums and assessments could increase and result in higher noninterest expense.
The failure of other financial institutions could adversely affect us, and we may incur losses on investments in other financial institutions.
The impacts of public health crises, including national or international pandemics, could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Risks Related to Our Business
Our decisions regarding credit risk could be inaccurate and our allowance for credit losses may be inadequate, which would materially and adversely affect us.
Our high concentration of real estate loans and especially commercial real estate loans exposes us to increased lending risk.
Our geographic concentration of banking activities and loan portfolio makes us more vulnerable to adverse conditions in our local markets.
If the value of real estate were to deteriorate, a significant portion of our loans could become under-collateralized, which could have a material adverse effect on us.
Because we have a concentration of exposure to a number of individual borrowers, a significant loss on any of those loans could materially and adversely affect us.
Our cost of funds may increase as a result of general economic conditions, interest rates and competitive pressures.
The loss of key employees may materially and adversely affect us.
The value of securities in our investment portfolio may decline in the future.
Our recent results do not indicate our future results and may not provide guidance to assess the risk of an investment in our common stock.
We may not be able to raise the additional capital we need to grow and, as a result, our ability to expand our operations could be materially impaired.
Our growth and expansion strategy may not be successful, and our market value and profitability may suffer.
If we acquire additional banks or bank assets in the future, there may be undiscovered risks or losses associated with such acquisitions which would have a negative impact upon our future income.
If the goodwill that we may record or have recorded in connection with a business acquisition becomes impaired, it could require charges to earnings.
Competition from other financial institutions and financial service providers may adversely affect our profitability.
We continually encounter technological change, and we may not be able to keep pace with rapid technological change in the financial services industry.
We may incur losses as a result of unforeseen or catastrophic events, including extreme weather events or other natural disasters.
We may incur environmental liabilities with respect to properties to which we take title.
Our operations could be interrupted if certain external vendors on which we rely experience difficulty, terminate their services or fail to comply with banking laws and regulations.
Our earnings could be adversely impacted by incidences of fraud and compliance failure.
Risks Related to the Proposed Acquisition of Mountain Commerce Bancorp, Inc.
We may fail to realize all of the anticipated benefits of the merger.

The completion of the merger is subject to the consent and approval of various governmental authorities, which may impose conditions that could have an adverse effect on the combined company following the merger.
The combined company expects to incur substantial expenses related to the merger.
Risks Related to Owning Our Stock
We may be unable to, or choose not to, pay dividends on our common stock.
paragraphs: Our business exposes us to certain risks. Risks and uncertainties that management is not aware of or focused on may also adversely affect our business and operation. The following is a discussion of the most significant risks and uncertainties that may affect our business, financial condition and future results.

We are subject to extensive regulation that could limit or restrict our activities and impose financial requirements or limitations on the conduct of our business, and changes in the laws and regulations to which we are subject could adversely affect our profitability.

We and our bank subsidiary are subject to extensive federal and state regulation and supervision. As a registered bank holding company, we are primarily regulated by the Federal Reserve Board. Our bank subsidiary is also primarily regulated by the Federal Reserve Board and the Arkansas State Bank Department.

Banking industry regulations are primarily intended to protect depositors' funds, federal deposit insurance funds and the banking system as a whole, not security holders. Complying with such regulations is costly and may limit our growth and restrict certain of our activities, including payment of dividends, mergers and acquisitions, investments, loans and interest rates charged, interest rates paid on deposits and locations of offices. We are also subject to capital requirements by our regulators. Violations of various laws, even if unintentional, may result in significant fines or other penalties, including restrictions on branching or bank acquisitions.

Congress and federal regulatory agencies continually review banking laws, regulations and policies for possible changes. While the federal regulatory agencies under the Trump Administration and current Congressional leadership are expected to exhibit a more common sense regulatory posture and pursue initiatives to reduce regulatory burdens on community and regional financial institutions, we cannot assure that future legislation or regulation will not significantly increase our compliance or operating costs or otherwise have a significant impact on our business. New federal or state laws, regulations and policies may continue to be enacted and implemented that could affect lending and funding practices and liquidity standards. Additionally, financial institution regulatory agencies may continue to aggressively scrutinize and address any concerns and trends identified in examinations, including through the issuance of formal enforcement actions. Negative developments in the financial services industry or other new legislation or regulations could adversely impact our operations and our financial performance by subjecting us to additional costs, restricting our business operations, including our ability to originate or sell loans, and/or increasing the ability of non-banks to offer competing financial services.

As regulation of the banking industry continues to evolve, the costs of compliance may continue to increase and, in turn, adversely affect our ability to operate profitably. In addition, industry, legislative or regulatory developments may cause us to materially change our existing strategic direction, capital strategies, compensation or operating plans. Further, any changes to or repeal of existing laws, regulations or policies relating to our business, as well as changes in interpretation, implementation or enforcement of such laws, regulations or policies, could affect us in substantial and unpredictable ways. Among other impacts, the repeal or revision of laws and regulations could necessitate that we implement new processes and procedures, which could divert management time and attention from initiatives designed to grow the Company or enhance our profitability. If any such developments negatively impact our ability to implement our business strategies, it may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and future prospects.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis presents our consolidated financial condition and results of operations for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023. This discussion should be read together with the "Summary Consolidated Financial Data," our consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto, and other financial data included in this document. In addition to the historical information provided below, we have made certain estimates and forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ significantly from those anticipated in these estimates and in the forward-looking statements as a result of certain factors, including those discussed in the section of this document captioned "Risk Factors," and elsewhere in this document. Unless the context requires otherwise, the terms "Company," "HBI," "us," "we" and "our" refer to Home BancShares, Inc. on a consolidated basis.

We are a bank holding company headquartered in Conway, Arkansas, offering a broad array of financial services through our wholly owned bank subsidiary, Centennial Bank ("Centennial" or the "Bank"). As of December 31, 2025, we had, on a consolidated basis, total assets of $22.88 billion, loans receivable, net, of $15.39 billion, total deposits of $17.48 billion, and stockholders' equity of $4.30 billion.

We generate most of our revenue from interest on loans and investments, service charges, and mortgage banking income. Deposits and Federal Home Loan Bank ("FHLB") borrowed funds are our primary source of funding. Our largest expenses are interest on our funding sources, salaries and related employee benefits and occupancy and equipment. We measure our performance by calculating our net interest margin, return on average assets and return on average common equity. We also measure our performance by our efficiency ratio and efficiency ratio, as adjusted (non-GAAP). The efficiency ratio is calculated by dividing non-interest expense less amortization of core deposit intangibles by the sum of net interest income on a tax equivalent basis and non-interest income. The efficiency ratio, as adjusted, is a meaningful non-GAAP measure for management, as it excludes certain items and is calculated by dividing non-interest expense less amortization of core deposit intangibles by the sum of net interest income on a tax equivalent basis and non-interest income excluding certain items such as merger expenses, hurricane expenses and/or gains and losses.

Our net income increased $73.2 million, or 18.2%, to $475.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, from $402.2 million for the same period in 2024. On a diluted earnings per share basis, our earnings were $2.41 per share for the year ended December 31, 2025 and $2.01 per share for the year ended December 31, 2024. The Company recorded $20.9 million in credit loss expense for the year ended December 31, 2025. This consisted of a $24.1 million provision for credit losses on loans, which was partially offset by a $2.2 million recovery of credit losses on available-for-sale investments and a $1.0 million recovery of credit losses on unfunded commitments. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded $7.4 million in special income from equity investments, a $2.4 million increase in the fair value of marketable securities, $2.0 million in recoveries on historic losses, a $1.9 million gain on the retirement of subordinated debentures, $1.5 million in income from a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC") assessment reduction, $1.4 million in bank owned life insurance ("BOLI") death benefits, a $983,000 gain on sale of a building from our Texas market and $885,000 in legal fee reimbursements, which were partially offset by $3.3 million in legal claims expense and $580,000 in merger expense.

paragraphs: Home BancShares, Inc. ("Home BancShares," "we," "us," "HBI" or the "Company") 為一間設於阿肯色州康韋市的銀行控股公司，已依照美國聯邦銀行控股公司法（Bank Holding Company Act of 1956）註冊。本公司普通股於紐約證券交易所交易，代碼為 "HOMB"。本公司主要從事提供廣泛的商業與零售銀行及相關金融服務，服務對象包括企業、不動產開發商與投資人、個人及地方政府，透過我們全資擁有之社區銀行子公司 – Centennial Bank。Centennial Bank 在阿肯色州、佛羅裏達州、德克薩斯州、南阿拉巴馬州及紐約市設有分行。雖然本公司擁有分散的貸款組合，但在 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日，商業不動產貸款分別佔總貸款的 53.2% 及 57.6%，並分別佔總股東權益的 194.3% 及 214.6%。本公司過去三年的總資產、總存款、總營業收入及淨收入如下：

Home BancShares 收購、組織並投資於服務具吸引力市場的社區銀行。我們的社區銀行團隊由經驗豐富的銀行家組成，並擁有強大的本地關係。本公司於 1998 年由由 John W. Allison（本公司董事長）及 Robert H. "Bunny" Adcock, Jr.（本公司董事之一）領導的投資者羣組所成立。自 1999 年開設我們的第一家子公司銀行以來，我們已收購並整合總共 23 家銀行，這些銀行位於阿肯色州、佛羅裏達州、德克薩斯州及阿拉巴馬州，其中 18 家是在 2010 年後收購，其中有 7 家是透過美國存款保險公司（FDIC）協助的交易收購。我們的子公司銀行自 2009 年起一直使用單一章程及 Centennial Bank 名稱運作。2015 年，我們在收購了一筆全國性的商業不動產貸款後，成立了 Centennial Commercial Finance Group（"Centennial CFG"），以建立一個專注於商業不動產貸款以及商業與工業貸款的全國性貸款平台。Centennial CFG 位於我們紐約市分行辦公室，並在加州洛杉機及德克薩斯州達拉斯設有貸款業務辦公室。2018 年，我們收購了 Shore Premier Finance（"SPF"），這是一家位於維吉尼亞州里士滿的 Union Bank & Trust 的船隻貸款部門，並設立了 SPF 分部於 Centennial Bank，以建立一個專注於商業與個人船隻貸款的貸款平台。2020 年，我們收購了 LH-Finance，這是一家位於康乃狄克州布里奇波特的 People's United Bank, N.A. 的船隻貸款部門，並將 LH-Finance 及其貸款組合與我們的 SPF 分部合併。SPF 分部在維吉尼亞州切薩皮克及馬裏蘭州巴爾的摩設有貸款業務辦公室。2022 年，我們完成了至今最大規模的收購，也是德克薩斯州首例，收購了位於德克薩斯州阿馬利洛的 Happy Bancshares, Inc. 及其銀行子公司 Happy State Bank，收購日期為 2022 年 4 月 1 日。
我們認為許多個人與企業偏好與由本地管理的社區銀行合作，因為這些銀行能提供靈活性與快速決策。我們執行社區銀行策略，使我們能迅速擴展銀行業務網路。以下摘要提供了過去五年財務年度中我們收購活動的更多細節。
LendingClub Bank 船隻貸款組合 – 2022 年 2 月 4 日，本公司完成了對位於猶他州的 LendingClub Bank（"LendingClub"）表現良好的船隻貸款組合的收購。根據與 LendingClub 簽訂的收購協議，本公司收購了約 2.422 億美元的遊艇貸款。這筆貸款組合由本公司 SPF 分部管理，並負責服務已收購的貸款組合及發放新貸款。

Happy Bancshares, Inc. – 2022 年 4 月 1 日，本公司完成了對 Happy Bancshares, Inc.（"Happy"）的收購，並將 Happy State Bank 合併至 Centennial Bank。本公司發行了約 4,240 萬股普通股，價值約 9.588 億美元（截至 2022 年 4 月 1 日）。此外，持有某些 Happy 股權獎勵的持有人獲得了約 370 萬美元現金，用以取消這些獎勵，總交易價值約為 9.625 億美元。
包含購併會計調整後，於取得日，Happy 約有總資產 6.69 十億美元，貸款 3.65 十億美元，以及客戶存款 5.86 十億美元。Happy 過去曾在德克薩斯州 62 個據點經營其銀行業務。
有關 Happy 取得之進一步討論，請參閱我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度年報 10-K 表單中「財務會計摘要」部分的第 2 節「企業合併」。

Mountain Commerce Bancorp, Inc. – 2025 年 12 月 7 日，本公司與 Centennial 籤訂與 Mountain Commerce Bancorp, Inc.（位於田納西州之公司，簡稱「MCBI」）及其 wholly-owned 銀行子公司 Mountain Commerce Bank（位於田納西州之州立銀行公司，簡稱「MCB」）之合併協議（簡稱「協議」），根據協議，本公司與 Centennial 將取得 MCBI 與 MCB。協議規定，透過一系列交易，本公司之子公司將與 MCBI 合併，MCBI 並將與本公司合併，本公司為存續公司（合稱「合併」）。合併後，MCB 將儘速與 Centennial 合併，Centennial 為存續公司。
依協議條款，本公司將於合併完成後，發行約 5.4 百萬股普通股，作為對 MCBI 股東的對價。合併過程中不會支付現金對價，除非在合併時持有 MCBI 普通股的股東，將會收到現金支票，以取代其應得的本公司普通股零碎股數。

根據協議條款，於合併生效時（簡稱「生效時」），每一股 MCBI 普通股將轉換為取得 0.85 股本公司普通股之權利（簡稱「合併對價」）。於生效時，所有未行權之 MCBI 普通股限制性股份將完全行權，並轉換為取得合併對價之權利。合併對價價值將以本公司普通股在紐約證券交易所之成交量加權平均收盤價計算，計算期間為合併閉幕前第三個營業日之 20 個連續交易日（簡稱「本公司平均收盤價」），再乘以 0.85。
合併預計於 2026 年第二季完成，並需經監管機構批准及其他協議中所載條件。
以下表格列示截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司高階主管之資訊。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析呈現本公司合併財務狀況及營運成果，為截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日之年度資料。此討論應與「彙總合併財務資料」、本公司合併財務報表及其附註，以及本文件中包含之其他財務資料一併閱讀。除下列所提供之歷史資訊外，本公司已做出某些估計與展望性陳述，這些陳述涉及風險與不確定性。本公司實際結果可能與這些估計及展望性陳述中預期的結果有顯著差異，原因包括本文件中標題為「風險因素」之部分及其他地方所討論之因素。除非上下文另有要求，否則「本公司」、「HBI」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」均指本公司於合併基礎上之Home BancShares, Inc。
本公司為一家總部設於阿肯色州康韋市的銀行控股公司，透過我們全資擁有之銀行子公司Centennial Bank（「Centennial」或「銀行」）提供廣泛之金融服務。截至2025年12月31日，本公司於合併基礎上擁有總資產228.8億美元、貸款應收款淨額153.9億美元、總存款174.8億美元，以及股東權益43.0億美元。

我們主要透過貸款及投資之利息、服務費用及房貸銀行收入產生營收。存款及美國聯邦住宅貸款銀行（「FHLB」）借款為我們主要資金來源。我們最大之費用為資金來源之利息、薪資及相關員工福利，以及營業場地及設備費用。我們以計算淨利息邊際率、平均資產回報率及平均普通股權益回報率來衡量表現。我們亦以效率比率及調整後效率比率（非GAAP）來衡量表現。效率比率係以非利息費用減去核心存款無形資產攤銷後除以淨利息收入（稅等價基礎）及非利息收入總和計算。調整後效率比率為管理層重要的非GAAP衡量指標，因其排除某些項目，並以非利息費用減去核心存款無形資產攤銷後除以淨利息收入（稅等價基礎）及非利息收入（排除某些項目如合併費用、颶風費用及/或損益）總和計算。

本公司淨收入增加 73.2 百萬美元，或 18.2%，至 475.4 百萬美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，較 2024 年同期的 402.2 百萬美元。以稀釋每股盈餘為基準，本公司 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年的盈餘為每股 2.41 美元，而 2024 年同期為每股 2.01 美元。本公司於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年計提 20.9 百萬美元的信用減損費用。此費用包含 24.1 百萬美元的貸款信用減損提撥，部分抵銷 2.2 百萬美元的可售證券信用減損回復，以及 1.0 百萬美元的未資金承諾信用減損回復。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年，本公司計入 7.4 百萬美元的權益投資特別收入，市場可交易證券公允價值增加 2.4 百萬美元，歷史減損回復 2.0 百萬美元，次級債權證券兌換收益 1.9 百萬美元，聯邦存款保險公司（"FDIC"）評估減免收入 1.5 百萬美元，銀行擁有壽險（"BOLI"）死亡保險金 1.4 百萬美元，德克薩斯市場建築物出售收益 983,000 美元，以及法律費用補償 885,000 美元，部分抵銷 3.3 百萬美元的法律索償費用及 580,000 美元的併購費用。

headings: 與我們產業相關的風險
因本公司總資產超過100億美元，我們面臨更嚴格的監管要求。
困難的市場與經濟環境可能對我們的產業與業務產生不利影響。
我們的FDIC保險費與評估金額可能增加，導致更高的非利息支出。
其他金融機構的失敗可能對我們產生不利影響，我們可能在對其他金融機構的投資中產生損失。
公共衛生危機的影響，包括國家或國際性的大流行病，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。
與我們業務相關的風險
我們對信用風險的判斷可能不正確，導致信用損失準備金不足，這將對我們產生重大且不利的影響。
本公司對不動產貸款，尤其是商業不動產貸款之高度集中，使我們面臨增加之貸款風險。
本公司銀行業務及貸款組合之地理集中，使我們更容易受到當地市場不利條件之影響。
若不動產價值惡化，我們貸款中之重大部分可能成為擔保不足，這可能會對我們造成重大不利影響。
由於我們對多數個別借款人之曝險集中，任何貸款之重大損失可能對我們造成重大且不利之影響。
因總體經濟情況、利率及競爭壓力，本公司之資金成本可能增加。
關鍵員工之流失可能對本公司造成重大且不利之影響。
本公司投資組閤中之證券價值可能於未來下跌。
本公司近期之營運成果並不能預示未來之營運成果，且可能無法提供評估投資本公司普通股之風險之參考。
我們可能無法籌措所需的額外資金以支應成長需求，因此本公司擴展營運能力可能受到重大影響。
本公司成長與擴張策略可能無法成功，並可能導致本公司市場價值與獲利能力受損。
若本公司未來取得其他銀行或銀行資產，可能伴隨未發現的風險或損失，對本公司未來收入造成負面影響。
若本公司因企業併購而記載或已記載之商譽價值減損，可能導致需對獲利課以減損費用。
來自其他金融機構及金融服務提供者的競爭可能對本公司獲利能力造成不利影響。
本公司持續面臨科技變革，可能無法跟上金融服務業快速的科技變革。
本公司可能因未預見或重大事件而產生虧損，包括極端天氣事件或其他自然災害。
本公司可能因取得財產所有權而產生環境責任。
本公司營運可能因我們所依賴之某些外部供應商遭遇困難、終止其服務或未能遵守銀行法規與法律而受影響。
本公司獲利可能因詐欺事件或合規失敗而受到不利影響。
與擬議收購 Mountain Commerce Bancorp, Inc. 相關的風險。
本公司可能無法實現合併所預期的全部好處。
合併之完成需經各政府主管機關之同意與批准，這些主管機關可能施加條件，對合併後之公司產生不利影響。
合併後之公司預期將產生與合併相關之重大支出。
與持有本公司股票相關的風險。
本公司可能無法或選擇不支付普通股股息。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨某些風險。管理層未察覺或未著重的風險與不確定性，也可能對本公司業務與營運造成不利影響。以下為可能影響本公司業務、財務狀況與未來結果的最重大風險與不確定性之討論。
本公司受廣泛規範，此等規範可能限制或限制本公司活動，並對本公司業務之進行施加財務要求或限制，且我們所受規範之法律與法規變動，可能對本公司獲利造成不利影響。
本公司與我們的銀行子公司均受廣泛聯邦與州政府規範與監督。作為已註冊之銀行控股公司，本公司主要受聯邦儲備委員會規範。我們的銀行子公司亦主要受聯邦儲備委員會與阿肯色州銀行部門規範。
銀行業規範主要旨在保護存款人資金、聯邦存款保險基金與整個銀行體系，而非股東。遵守此等規範成本高昂，可能限制我們的成長，並限制某些活動，包括支付紅利、合併與收購、投資、貸款與所收取之利率、支付存款之利率與辦事處所在地。我們亦受我們監管機構之資本要求所規範。即使為非故意，違反各種法律，可能導致重大罰款或其他處罰，包括限制分支機構或銀行收購。

國會與聯邦監管機構持續審查銀行法規、法規與政策，以考量可能之變動。雖然在川普政府與現任國會領袖之下，聯邦監管機構預期會展現較為務實之監管姿態，並推動減少對社區與區域性金融機構之監管負擔之倡議，我們無法保證未來立法或法規不會顯著增加我們之合規或營運成本，或以其他方式對本公司業務產生重大影響。新的聯邦或州法律、法規與政策可能持續被制定與實施，此等法規可能影響貸款與資金運用做法與流動性標準。此外，金融機構監管機構可能持續嚴格審查並處理在檢查中所識別出之任何關注點與趨勢，包括透過發布正式之處罰行動。金融服務業之負面發展或其他新立法或法規，可能對本公司營運與財務表現造成不利影響，透過增加成本、限制本公司業務營運，包括本公司發放或出售貸款之能力，以及/或增加非銀行機構提供競爭性金融服務之能力。

隨著銀行業規範持續演進，合規成本可能持續增加，進而對本公司獲利能力造成不利影響。此外，產業、立法或監管發展可能導致本公司大幅改變現有戰略方向、資本策略、薪酬或營運計畫。進一步而言，任何對現有法律、法規或政策之變動或廢除，以及對此等法律、法規或政策之解釋、執行或強制執行之變動，可能以重大且難以預測之方式影響本公司。其中可能影響包括，廢除或修訂法律與法規可能導致本公司必須實施新程序與作業流程，此可能使管理階層時間與注意力從旨在成長本公司或提升獲利能力之計畫中被分散。若任何此等發展對本公司執行業務策略之能力造成負面影響，可能對本公司營運結果與未來前景產生重大不利影響。
